title: Model Configuration
summary: Assign Main and optional Helper in Inference or Settings → Model routing. Each role can use a different provider, model, context ceiling, API key and generation profile. Additional.
html:
Model configuration and routing

Assign Main and Helper

Assign Main and optional Helper in Inference or Settings → Model routing. Each role can use a different provider, model, context ceiling, API key and generation profile. Additional installed models and managed instance profiles remain available for later assignment.

An optional Vision connection in Settings → Model routing serves explicit OCR and image-analysis calls. With Vision unassigned, those routes use Main. The active endpoint must advertise image input; names alone do not establish capability. Each Vision task uses its captured configuration and normal inference budget. See attachments and Vision for authorized sources, dependency placement and coverage limits.

The composer follows the global configuration. Its thinking and output controls tune agent decisions without changing model assignments.

Each role has an Auto-select model toggle. When on, new requests use the first model reported by that role's endpoint. Manual model entry and discovery controls are disabled; the endpoint, API key and generation settings remain editable. Turn Auto off to enter or discover a specific model, then use Save Main or Save Helper. New configurations start with Auto on; saved model names keep it off.

Settings provides a destination and Allow fallback to Main for each supported call:

  • Agent decisions and final answers: Main.
  • Fresh agent recovery: Main.
  • Task-contract compilation: Helper.
  • Task-contract retries and corrections: Main.
  • Automatic capability selection: Helper.
  • Schedule drafting, monitor drafting, monitor judgments and parameter drafting: Helper.
  • Vision OCR and visual understanding: Vision, or Main when Vision is unassigned.

With no Helper configured, Helper rows with fallback enabled use Main. Disable fallback when a call must use Helper. A missing or unavailable strict Helper produces an actionable error.

A configured Vision route can fall back once to Main on an eligible failure when its fallback setting allows it. Main must also advertise image input. A failed Vision connection followed by text-only Main retains the connection/capability failure rather than implying that the attached image is missing. An unassigned Vision role resolves to Main even when transport fallback is disabled.

Generation and context controls belong to each role. Provider Default omits optional provider parameters; Custom lets you configure them individually. Provider support is negotiated separately for each endpoint. Saving one role preserves the other role's saved configuration and draft edits. A concurrent edit reports a revision conflict instead of silently replacing newer settings.

smTO Recommended resolves a starting preset when you save the role. That saved parameter map stays fixed for accepted work; changing a recommendation later does not rewrite it. Unknown provider/model combinations use the common small-agent preset, with unsupported optional fields handled by wire compatibility negotiation. An explicit zero, false or empty list in Custom is a configured value, not the same as leaving that parameter at Provider Default. Internal phases can impose their own output and thinking policy on the selected role.

Saving Main or Helper refreshes model discovery for new requests, including when a different model replaces the previous one at the same endpoint. With Context ceiling left blank (Auto), new requests use the server's reported context capacity.

Output limit and context space

The provider's output limit and smTO's internal output reservation serve different purposes. Provider Default may omit an output limit from the request, while smTO still reserves space for the answer when preparing input and conversation history. An explicit completion-token limit (max_completion_tokens) becomes the execution reservation. Increasing it leaves less room for input within the same context window.

If a request does not fit, inspect the selected model's context ceiling and output settings together. A large output allowance does not increase the model's context capacity. See context and memory for how retained conversation material is projected into a request.

Thinking effort and budget

Thinking On/Off, reasoning effort and a thinking-token budget are separate provider controls. Their availability depends on the selected endpoint and model. An explicit Thinking choice uses the model template's enable_thinking setting; reasoning effort does not universally mean the same thing. Provider Default leaves optional choices to the provider.

Task Contract compilation and recovery use their own saved thinking policies. Changing normal execution settings does not replace those policies. See Task Contract thinking for the compilation-specific controls.

Force budget and stop thinking is off by default. When enabled, the next normal execution decision can send its numeric thinking target to a server whose control support has been detected. A completion-token limit is required, and the target must leave space for the answer. Unknown support produces an availability notice; the setting does not establish support by itself. For llama.cpp, smTO checks advertised capabilities or guarded zero-token validation requests, independently of the server's build hash. Results refresh periodically at execution decisions. Compiler and selection phases keep their own policy.

With forcing off, an eligible llama.cpp stream can offer a live stop-thinking control after it exceeds the soft target. That action addresses the current completion while its response continues; it does not start a replacement task or execute partial tool arguments. An acknowledgement is distinct from an observed stop. Changing the global toggle affects the next decision, while an active response and its output-limit continuations retain their policy.

The live button is labeled Stop reasoning and act…. While its request is pending, it shows Stopping reasoning… and prevents duplicate clicks for that attempt. An unavailable or replaced attempt removes the action. If the request fails and the same attempt is still eligible, the page offers retry and explains that the response is still running. The task's Stop control remains the way to stop the task; the reasoning button requests a transition within the current response.

Automatic budget increases

When normal execution rejects an incomplete model response because its output was truncated, smTO can reserve a larger output allowance and retry the pending decision. The default policy permits three consecutive increases of 1,000 output tokens each. The rejected partial response is not executed. Cancellation, exhausted run budgets, provider limits and insufficient context capacity can prevent an increase.

An unknown provider output limit cannot be guessed from usage counts. An explicit limit reported by the provider can establish the starting allowance. A provider- rejected increase restores the last usable allowance; the attempted increase remains counted. Accepting a complete response resets the consecutive-increase counter while retaining the effective output allowance for that conversation.

The thinking percentage is a soft target; it does not trigger this output-retry mechanism. Internal model phases do not use these execution-only overrides.

Tool-call repetition

Open Settings → Setup → Model routing → Tool-call repetition to configure protection against unfinished tool calls that keep generating the same data.

  • Stop extreme tool-call repetition is on by default.
  • Minimum repeated characters defaults to 16,384; allowed range: 2,048–65,536.
  • Minimum repetitions defaults to 8; allowed range: 4–32.

Both thresholds must be met across two consecutive checks. Higher values allow larger repetitive payloads. Deliberately repeated data can also trigger the guard; use compact code to generate it or adjust these controls for your workload.

Changes save automatically and apply at the next model call, including active tasks and task-contract compilation. A response already in progress keeps its settings. Turning this switch off preserves the threshold values and leaves reasoning-loop and inactivity protection unchanged. The Generation quality check must also be enforced for this guard to interrupt a response. Rejected partial calls do not execute; the existing bounded recovery policy still applies.

Accepted tasks and diagnostics

Accepted tasks keep their configuration while running, queued or paused. New prompts, follow-ups, scheduled runs and workflow runs use current settings. A failed Helper request may fall back once to Main before accepting a complete response; context is rebuilt using Main's limits. Cancellation and exhausted budgets prevent fallback. Fresh recovery can use another role; continuation of an unfinished response stays on its original model.

Saving routing settings does not require a controller restart. A later API-key change applies to new work; an accepted task retains its captured credential version. Removing Helper likewise does not rewrite a task's accepted snapshot.

Use Check saved model on a role's card to test that model directly. Diagnostics never fall back. Task traces and the Inference timeline display the actual model, call type, revision and fallback reason.

Task summaries, context compaction and tool execution remain local operations. They have no model-routing rows.

Local AI runtimes

The optional Local AI Runtimes skill manages model servers on the selected Gateway using accepted Parameter profiles. Starting one leaves model assignments unchanged. Its explicit preview/activate/restore workflow can update Main through revisioned routing for future work; accepted tasks retain their configuration. See Gateway Local AI runtimes for setup, provider limits, credential/reachability requirements and recovery. The controller's Inference area owns its separate installation and instance UI.
